look_for: Starts from what real users did or said, changes the plan because of it, and checks whether it helped.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you changed what you were building because of what users told you, or what you saw them do.
followups: How did you find out what they actually needed?
What did you change, and what did it cost you?
How did you know the change helped them?

questions.q: Tell me about something you built that people didn't use the way you expected. What did you do about it?
followups: When did you realize it wasn't working?
What did you do about it yourself?
What would you do differently from the start?

look_for: Makes an unclear problem concrete, decides what they can on their own, and owns the outcome.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you had to deliver something when the requirements were unclear or kept changing.
followups: What did you do first to make it less unclear?
What did you decide on your own, and why?
How did it turn out?

questions.q: Tell me about a time you noticed a problem that nobody owned, and you fixed it yourself.
followups: How did you notice it?
Why did you take it on instead of just flagging it?
What happened as a result?

lp: Working across teams and time zones
look_for: Works well with people who are far away or think differently: adapts how they communicate, writes things down, and gets to a shared decision.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you worked with people in a different time zone, language, or background to get something done.
followups: What made it hard?
What did you change about how you communicated?
What would you keep doing the same way next time?

questions.q: Tell me about a time you worked closely with a designer, a product manager, or someone outside engineering, and you saw things differently.
followups: What did they want that you didn't, at first?
How did you get to a decision?
What did you learn about working with them?

look_for: Disagrees with evidence, listens to the other side, commits to the decision, and takes feedback without getting defensive.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate or your lead about a technical decision.
followups: What was your argument, and what was theirs?
How did you handle the disagreement?
What happened in the end, and would you do it the same way again?

questions.q: Tell me about a time you got critical feedback on your work.
followups: What exactly was the feedback?
How did you react at first?
What did you change because of it?

look_for: Gets productive quickly in something new: has a way of learning, asks for help at the right time, and knows what they still don't know.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you had to learn a new technology or codebase quickly to deliver something.
followups: How did you go about learning it?
What was hardest to get right?
How long did it take before you were productive?

questions.q: Tell me about a time you were stuck on a problem for a long time. How did you get unstuck?
followups: What had you already tried?
When did you ask for help, and who did you ask?
What do you do differently now when you're stuck?

look_for: Owns a real mistake or failure, says plainly what their part was, fixes it, and changes something so it doesn't happen again.

questions.q: Tell me about a time something you shipped broke or didn't work. What happened?
followups: How did you find out?
What did you do first?
What did you change so it wouldn't happen again?

questions.q: Tell me about a project that failed, or one you'd do completely differently now.
followups: What went wrong, and what was your part in it?
When did you realize it?
What do you do differently today because of it?

look_for: Under time pressure, picks what matters, cuts scope on purpose, says who they told, and manages the risk of shipping early.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you had more to do than time to do it. How did you decide what to cut?
followups: What were the options?
What did you cut, and who did you tell?
How did it turn out?

questions.q: Tell me about a time you shipped something quickly that wasn't perfect. How did you decide it was good enough?
followups: What did you leave out on purpose?
How did you lower the risk?
What happened after it shipped?

look_for: Improves something nobody asked them to, gets other people to use it, and can say what changed because of it.

questions.q: Tell me about something you built or improved that nobody asked you to.
followups: Why did you think it was worth doing?
How did you get people to use it?
What changed because of it?

questions.q: Tell me about a time you made a process or a tool better for the people you worked with.
followups: What was slow or painful before?
What did you change yourself?
How did you know it was better?
